title: ActualSurface
description: What a codebase REALLY exposes, in manifest vocabulary. Produced by a per-stack adapter (Rust: syn; JVM: annotation scan; Node: router table), consumed by `rqunit conformance`, which owns the diff against the manifest. Adapters extract and never judge: no adapter decides what a divergence means.

generated_by.description: Adapter name and version — the report attributes findings to their extractor.

services.description: Keyed by manifest service slug. A service absent here is not reconciled at all (no adapter covers it); a service present with empty surfaces asserts the code exposes nothing.

access.description: Structural access tier as the code composes it (which middleware stack the route is mounted under). Membership in access_tiers is the manifest's business, not the adapter's.

direction.description: Optional: adapters that cannot determine direction omit it, and the reconciler falls back to presence-only matching.

exceptions.description: Divergences the consumer has ratified at Gate 1. They travel INSIDE the artifact so they are reviewable data, never a constant buried in adapter code — and the reconciler still REPORTS each one as a justified finding rather than silencing it.

rule.description: Which divergence class this exception excuses.

target.description: Identifies the surface: '<METHOD> <path>' for endpoints, the subject for messages.

justification.description: Why the divergence is correct. Mandatory and substantive: an exception nobody can defend in prose is a defect wearing a waiver.
